Consult Summary:
- Male patient with 3 days of frequent watery, non-bloody diarrhea (6–7/day), intermittent left lower abdominal cramping, initial vomiting and subjective fever after restaurant meal; currently tolerating fluids; clinical impression is acute gastroenteritis with conservative management advised (oral rehydration, acetaminophen, rest, reassess if not improved in 3–4 days).

History:
- Presenting complaint: Diarrhea for 3 days affecting daily activities; needs to stay near a toilet.
- Symptom details:
  - Diarrhea: Loose, watery stools, ~6–7 times/day; no blood or mucus reported.
  - Abdominal pain: Intermittent cramp-like pain in the left lower abdomen; does not radiate to the back.
  - Systemic/associated: Felt hot at symptom onset (subjective fever) 3–4 days ago; initial vomiting (now resolved); loss of appetite; feels weak/shaky; no current fever reported; fluids tolerated.
  - Diet during illness: Primarily soups, smoothies, and light foods; able to maintain oral fluids.
- Triggers/exposures:
  - Ate at a Chinese restaurant (takeaway/dine-out) ~4 days ago; symptoms began ~1 day later.
  - One child at home had vomiting (no diarrhea); no other household members ill.
- Course/timeline:
  - Day 0–1: Restaurant meal; onset of symptoms ~1 day later with vomiting and feeling hot.
  - Days 1–3: Persistent watery diarrhea and intermittent LLQ cramps; vomiting resolved; continues to feel weak; maintaining fluids.
- Impact on function: Continued to work as an accountant but finds it difficult due to frequent bowel movements.
- Pertinent negatives: No blood in stool; no hematemesis; no known chronic bowel disease; no current fever; no night sweats mentioned.
- Systems review: As above; other systems not discussed.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma:
  - Background: Well-controlled.
  - Medications: Uses an inhaler (type/dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - No complications reported.
- No other chronic conditions reported.
- Medications (current): Asthma inhaler as above; no other routine medications.
- Allergies: Not discussed.

Social History:
- Lives with wife and two children.
- Occupation: Accountant; has continued working during illness.
- Tobacco: Never smoker.
- Alcohol: Does not drink alcohol.
- Recent food exposure: Chinese restaurant meal ~4 days ago.

Family History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed/not documented.

Investigations:
- None obtained/discussed during this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute gastroenteritis (likely viral; bacterial foodborne also possible)
  - Assessment:
    - Short-duration watery, non-bloody diarrhea with intermittent crampy LLQ pain.
    - Initial vomiting and subjective fever; tolerating fluids now.
    - Temporal association with restaurant meal; household contact with vomiting.
    - No red flags documented (no blood in stool, no ongoing vomiting).
  - Plan:
    - Oral hydration: Encourage fluids; use oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) especially in the first few days.
    - Symptomatic treatment: Acetaminophen (paracetamol) “two tablets up to four times a day” for a few days if feeling feverish/weak (dose/strength not documented).
    - Activity/work: Rest; advised to take 2–3 days off work.
    - Follow-up: If symptoms have not improved in 3–4 days, return for reassessment; may require stool testing at that time.
    - Antibiotics: Not indicated at present.
- Issue 2: Asthma – well controlled
  - Assessment: No current respiratory complaints; no exacerbation reported.
  - Plan: No changes discussed.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Acute viral gastroenteritis (likely norovirus) – High likelihood
  - Reasoning: Short, self-limited watery diarrhea with initial vomiting and subjective fever; possible household contact with vomiting; tolerating fluids.
- Acute bacterial gastroenteritis/foodborne infection (e.g., Salmonella, ETEC, Campylobacter) – Moderate likelihood
  - Reasoning: Onset ~1 day after restaurant meal; watery diarrhea with crampy abdominal pain and early fever; absence of blood does not exclude.
- Toxin-mediated food poisoning (Staphylococcus aureus, Bacillus cereus) – Low likelihood
  - Reasoning: Restaurant exposure and early vomiting fit, but typical incubation is hours and illness is shorter than 3 days.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Vitals and physical examination not documented.
  - Allergies not documented.
  - Asthma inhaler type/strength/frequency not documented.
  - Objective temperature not measured; subjective fever only.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None significant. Fever was subjective at onset; no measured fever currently.
- Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor pauses but no inaudible segments affecting clinical content.
